column3: Gives the compact witness/present-witness pairing that sharpens the public-presence aspect of the focus.
Offers a messenger-with-signs scene, but adds no clear household or witness relation.
Makes witnessing a messenger's public office, a strong parallel to presence as accountable evidence.
Directly pairs extended means with sons, closely paralleling the endowment sequence around 74:13.
Opens the addressed commission whose contrast with the endowed opponent frames the local passage.
Presents the messenger as witness over a community, supplying a direct responsibility dimension to witnessed presence.
Lists sons among bestowed supports, independently confirming the provision register without fixing its evaluation.
Immediately continues the catalogue by stressing made-ready ease, so it completes the local grant sequence.
Supplies divine witnessing as confirmation of a public claim, rather than a household-specific parallel.
Places wealth and sons among increase and provision; useful, though it repeats the grant pattern already established.
Moves the local discourse toward the trumpet event, setting the later reckoning behind the catalogue of gifts.
Shows witnessing as privileged presence around a record, extending the focus's possible evidentiary dimension.
Joins wealth and sons to restored collective strength, adding a historical-political use of the same endowment pair.
Combines named kin relations with divine witnessing, but its access rules do not explain the focus directly.
States comprehensive divine witnessing, a broad ground for the focus's possible accountability pressure.
Questions whether wealth and sons should be read as unqualified favor, a crucial contrary reading of the local gifts.
The command to warn establishes the commission against which the endowed figure's response is assessed.
Turns bodily traces into testimony, supporting a reading in which visible presence can become evidence.
Links every undertaking to present witnessing and a complete record, giving the strongest accountability analogue.
Immediately exposes the recipient's demand for further increase, preventing the gifts from reading as a closed blessing.
Connects rejection of signs with divine witnessing of deeds, a relevant but less specific accountability parallel.
Uses self-witness in relation to blameworthy response, supporting the focus's pressure of visible self-evidence.
Begins the opponent's calculating response, supplying the internal turn that follows the catalogue of endowments.
Divine witnessing secures a messenger's recompense, but the economic setting differs from household provision.
Joins a son reference to testimony limited by knowledge, preserving a distinct boundary on what witnessing can establish.
Names an assembled, witnessed day, supplying the public eschatological horizon behind accountable presence.
Sets communal witnesses beside a clarifying book, expanding the focus from family visibility to public evidence.
Places sons in a witnessed final family exchange, adding lineage and succession rather than material endowment.
The command to magnify the Lord helps distinguish the source of the gifts from their recipient.
Portrays testimony as something maintained, adding a durable public-duty sense to witness language.
Makes agents present over their own acts, a close parallel to presence that itself bears incriminating force.
Its warning against seeking more belongs to the local increase theme and counterbalances acquisitive readings.
Places visible action under multiple observers and final disclosure, a secondary accountability analogue.
Shows sons among ties abandoned at the decisive moment, a contrary limit on their enduring protective value.
Identifies obstinate rejection of the signs as the reason the local catalogue leads to threat rather than honor.
Models testimony as ordered with knowledge and justice, but remains abstract relative to the focus.
The oath by Sinai has no discernible relation to sons, presence, or the local endowment sequence.
The call to stand and reflect loosely parallels the opponent's deliberation but adds little to 74:13.
A community witness forecloses later repair, strengthening the consequence side of visible accountability.
The drink-mixture detail has no usable relation to the focus.
Part of the commission's preparatory commands, providing local contrast but no direct household evidence.
Links guarding a revealed book with witnessing, a secondary model of entrusted public responsibility.
The mention of speech organs does not materially clarify 74:13.
Supplies the preceding grant of extended wealth, the first half of the immediate paired endowment.
Combines the trumpet horizon with knowledge of hidden and manifest, supporting later evaluation of visible gifts.
Shares an extended-form expression only; it adds no comparable endowment or witness relation.
Introduces the singularly created recipient of the following gifts, anchoring 74:13 in its local portrait.
Frames contested revelation through summoned witnesses, a distinct evidentiary setting rather than a household parallel.
Supplies a punishment image that can illuminate the local threat, though not the focus itself.
The clear book motif is too remote from the household-presence theme.
Challenges concealed testimony and claims of knowledge, preserving an epistemic boundary relevant to witness language.
Uses building imagery rather than offspring, so the lexical overlap has little interpretive force.
Completes the commission's separation from defilement, a local contrast to the recipient's later refusal.
Pairs knowledge of hidden and manifest, a broad framework for judging what visible household status does and does not show.
A later facial state only weakly supplements the local warning sequence.
States the immediate threatened burden, showing the reversal that follows the endowed status.
Defines a community and messenger through reciprocal witnessing, a strong public analogue to accountable presence.
Uses witnesses in a legal procedure, but offers no close relation to the focus's household setting.
Directly specifies the severe day for the rejecters, completing the nearby consequence frame.
Contrasts divine testimony with competing claims and joins it to warning, relevant but more general than earlier witness cards.
Uses witnessed presence in a calendrical rule, not in the focus's social or evidentiary register.
Shows signs met with laughter, a remote parallel to rejection without a household link.
Combines acknowledged covenant with being witnesses, adding a self-implicating testimony pattern.
Places sons within a polemical allocation question, preserving a contrary use of filial language.
The command to persevere for the Lord completes the commission-side contrast within the surah.
Places a messenger's witness at final judgment, but this repeats the witness-office pattern at lower marginal value.
Joins descendants to self-witness and later accountability, adding a distinct generational dimension.
Shows a disclosed number becoming a test of responses, a later surah parallel to signs exposing inner disposition.
Stages a public summons to witness, distinguishing visibility from proof in a way relevant to witnessed presence.
Mentions witnesses amid changing fortunes, but does not connect them to household endowment.
The opposition to each prophet only broadly resembles the local hostile recipient.
Treats a group's own manifested disbelief as testimony against itself, a close self-evidence counterpart.
Develops documentary legal testimony, useful only as a distant formal witness analogue.
Names that day as difficult, directly reinforcing the consequence already signaled beside the focus.
Pairs hidden and manifest within divine knowledge, an abstract support for not equating appearance with full judgment.
Addresses obstruction undertaken while knowing, a secondary model of witness-conscious resistance.
The alteration command lacks a clear link to sons or witnessing in 74:13.
Challenges claims made without witnessed authority, adding a boundary against unsupported assertion.
Combines an Israelite witness with lineage language, but its cross-community proof setting is distinct.
General clear signs and admonition offer only a broad disclosure context.
Returns all persons to the knower of hidden and manifest for disclosure, extending the final-account horizon.
Uses witnesses for an entrusted property transfer, a peripheral public-accountability parallel.
The prohibited-act list does not illuminate the focus.
Forbids concealing testimony, but the transactional setting is remote from 74:13.
Seeks inclusion among witnesses without clarifying presence, sons, or the local reversal.
An elevated constructed sign concerns display, not the filial endowment in the focus.
Links support to the day witnesses stand, adding a final vindication motif after earlier direct witness parallels.
Makes a covenant publicly witnessed, a secondary form of accountable acknowledgment.
The construction reference has no meaningful relation to 74:13.
Lets the body's surface testify against its owner, a vivid extension of visible form as evidence.
The command to build a structure is unrelated to the focus beyond a lexical root.
Requires public attendance at a penalty, a limited procedural analogue to witnessed consequence.
The simile does not add to the focus.
Separates witness-language from truthful inner commitment, a key contrary check on merely public testimony.
Repeats the messenger-as-witness and warner office already supplied earlier, with reduced marginal value.
Pairs prior warning with self-testimony at judgment, reinforcing accountability but repeating earlier self-witness evidence.
The preservation of recitation has no clear connection to the focus.
Divine witnessing exposes a claimed intention as false against visible effects, a secondary anti-appearance parallel.
General kin obligations do not clarify the specific sons-as-present endowment.
Gathers forgotten acts into an exhaustive witnessed account, a strong theme but largely redundant after 10:61.
Pairs a garden-holder's resources and sons with a corrective comparison, directly testing status claims built from such gifts.
Treats wealth and children as worldly adornment while ranking enduring good deeds otherwise, a central contrary reading of the endowment.
Has a prosperous group invoke wealth and sons as grounds for exemption, closely paralleling the self-assessment exposed in the local passage.
Explicitly blocks reading wealth and children as honor by placing them within a punitive process.
Warns that wealth and children can divert from remembrance, supplying a direct functional risk for the gifts.
Names wealth and children as a test, a compact interpretive check on the local catalogue.
Likewise casts property and children as a trial, independently reinforcing the non-automatic reading of endowment.
Places sons among what a guilty person would offer to escape the day, showing the limit of filial value under judgment.
Sets increase in wealth and children within a transient worldly competition, a broad but relevant contrary frame.
Lists children among attractive human desires, clarifying the desire register without determining the focus's evaluation.
Denies that wealth and children can avail against God, adding an eschatological limit to their apparent security.
Repeats the non-availing wealth-and-children pattern, with lower marginal value after 3:10.
Again denies protection through wealth and children, a final-account counterpart to the local threat.
Returns to wealth and children as a means of distress; it reinforces 9:55 but adds little beyond it.
Shows wealth and families invoked as a preoccupation, a distinct way household assets can obstruct response.
Frames offspring within divine sovereignty over bestowal, supporting the gift-source side without the focus's witness term.
Completes the differentiated bestowal of sons and daughters, retaining a positive grant reading alongside the warnings.
Places offspring within household formation and provision, a constructive domestic parallel to sons made present.
Includes children within a corrupting partnership claim, a contrary account of how family extension can be used.
Denies that parent or child can answer for the other on the decisive day, limiting familial security.
Presents offspring within a prayer for household consolation and leadership, preserving a positive household reading alongside the warnings.
Addresses children in a provision-and-protection context, showing their vulnerability rather than their status value.
Returns to provision for children amid fear of want, relevant to dependence but not to witnessed presence.
Condemns destructive claims involving children, a remote warning against treating offspring as disposable property.
Uses children in inheritance allocation, supplying legal household structure rather than the focus's rhetorical function.
Brings a witness from every community and the messenger as witness, a major final-account analogue omitted from the list.
Uses a witness from the household to resolve a contested claim, closely joining kin space and evidentiary presence.
Makes tongues, hands, and feet testify about what was done, a complementary bodily-evidence passage to 36:65 and 41:21.
Sets the book, prophets, and witnesses within the final judgment scene, extending the evidentiary horizon of the focus.
Makes hearing, sight, and skins testify against their owner, supplying the fuller bodily-witness scene.
Pairs each soul with a driver and witness at arrival for judgment, a concise accountability counterpart.
Makes the person evidence against himself, sharpening the self-implicating reading of visible status and response.
Defines witnessing as presence over a community during one's stay, a close temporal sense for the focus's present language.
States divine witnessing over all things, a broad support now largely redundant with earlier universal-witness cards.
Uses God as sufficient witness between disputants, a claim-validation counterpart with limited household relevance.
Connects testimony to recording and later questioning, adding a record-and-account dimension.
Presents a record that speaks with truth at judgment, parallel evidence though it lacks the witness lexeme.
Connects faithful testimony with reward and light, preserving a positive, non-accusatory witness reading.
Uses four witnesses as an evidentiary threshold, a procedural witness model distant from the focus.
Frames a spouse's repeated testimony, another legal form with little direct relation to sons made present.
Requires witnesses for an accusation, reinforcing proof standards but not the local endowment sequence.
Requires upright witnesses at a separation, a household-adjacent procedural use with limited explanatory value.
